personalProjects.name: Observability Platform
personalProjects.description: Homelab infrastructure metrics and logs were scattered per-service, slowing root-cause analysis during incidents. Scraped Proxmox VM/CT metrics via Prometheus node_exporter, ingested logs via Loki Promtail, and managed Grafana dashboard definitions as code (Grafana-as-code) for IaC-reproducible deployment. PromQL + LogQL cross-queries in Grafana Explore unify metrics and logs in a single analysis surface.

personalProjects.name: n8n Automation
personalProjects.description: Repetitive operations — Slack notifications, Cloudflare deploy alerts, GitHub Actions result collection — were scattered across crontab and ad-hoc scripts, requiring code changes for every new integration. Onboarded n8n as central orchestrator wiring Slack, GitHub, Cloudflare, and Grafana via webhook+API, abstracting error handling and retry into shared workflow nodes. New automations deploy by adding nodes, not writing scripts; Slack alerts, GitHub Actions collection, and Cloudflare deploy hooks all run on the same workflow base.

personalProjects.name: Security Alert System
personalProjects.description: FortiGate security events were scattered across device syslog and Splunk, delaying the time from event occurrence to operator awareness. Connected Splunk Saved Search webhooks to Slack/Telegram so security events are immediately notified upon detection. Reduced security event awareness time and standardized operator response flow.

personalProjects.name: IP Blacklist Platform

Multiple threat feeds queryable and cross-analyzable from a reproducible pipeline.

en.headline: From OA to Security — Trajectory Participated in building on One Conviction
paragraphs: My career started inside Korea Aerospace Industries' closed network, tracking patch schedules for the closed-network Linux fleet on an Excel sheet. Repeating the same operations every week led to a single conviction: the value of security operations is not maintaining zero incidents, but automating the guarantee of zero incidents. I spent the next 11 months consecutively earning RHCSA, LPIC-1, and Linux Master Level 2 to rebuild my Linux foundation, then carried that into eight years of operations.

At Metanet M Platform I first picked up Ansible and Python, cutting NAC policy deployment for a large-scale contact center via Ansible automation. At Jointree, I applied NSX-T microsegmentation to Kookmin University's next-generation information system, eliminating east-west traffic blind spots — blocking ongoing intrusion attempts and reducing DLP false positives. The tools changed, but the principle didn't: any task that requires hands is a candidate for automation.

At Quantec Investment Management's Financial Security Data Center (FSDC), responding to Financial Supervisory Service audits taught me that security operations ultimately means "can you prove it to an auditor with data?" Tuning DB access-control queries to materially lower CPU load and validating a PB platform POC were both expressions of one goal: defensible operations.

Today I am embedded in the Nextrade exchange security track, continuously engaged from build (Gaonnuri) into operations (ITCEN CTS). I designed FortiGate HA with 5-tier network segmentation, passed the FSC licensing review, standardized security appliance configuration with Ansible Role (firewall policies standardized via Ansible Role), and operate Splunk ES detection rules + n8n + FortiManager API automated response with automated detection and response. The environment covers the exchange security environment.

Next, I want to integrate AI agents with Edge runtimes. My homelab — Cloudflare Workers, MCP, Grafana, 1Password — runs on Terraform-managed IaC where I validate "AI handles the first pass of security operations toil" patterns. I want to spend my next chapter not operating the tools that exist, but answering operational problems with new tools.
en.closing: I'd like to bring this trajectory — built on a single question about the limits of repetitive work — to the next problem your security infrastructure needs to solve.
